doors.trait: Relying on yourself hardens into refusal when another person offers a hand with work you have already claimed. At six in the evening, the shared document still carries only your edits. You can do the work. Accepting help would mean letting a different standard touch yours, and that is where you draw the line.

doors.scene: At ten, an invitation sits beside the schedule you wrote for the evening. You can keep every planned task and still have time for nothing that arrived unplanned. Crossing out a line feels harder than turning down the company, even when the rule has little left to protect.

doors.trait: Letting people in stopped being something you decline and became something you cannot quite locate. Fine, you say, on the day of the diagnosis, the layoff, the breakup. The word has three hundred uses now, and not one of them means fine.

doors.scene: A friend was in town for one evening, the first in three years. Lights out at eleven held anyway, the way it held through the fever, the way it holds through everything. You slept on schedule and lay there knowing exactly what the schedule had cost.
